title: Geometric, higher-image and restriction data for equivariant proper pushforward
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. An affine finite-type group scheme is a group object $G$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sc-group-scheme] with affine underlying scheme and finite-type structure morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. An action space is any $k$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] with a left $G$-action; it is finite separated if its structure map is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A proper equivariant map is an actual map over $k$ respecting these actions and proper on schemes. Use the action-groupoid models, coherent categories, underlying modules and normalized linearizations, integral Grothendieck groups and class maps of [def-sfb-equivariant-coherent-gzero], and the rational modules, representation groups and associated-bundle predicate of [def-sfb-rational-representation-gzero]; none is constructed again. Higher direct images are the existing Zariski module higher direct-image functors of [def-pc-derived-direct-image], using the standard derived localization. A closed subgroup is a closed immersion of affine finite-type group schemes respecting multiplication and unit. Restriction retains the same underlying scheme, replaces its action by the composite with $H\to G$, and retains the same module up to an isomorphism intertwining descent with its pullback along $H\times X\to G\times X$, with the section-normalized pullback compositors [def-pc-module-pullback]. The point is $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with the unique action, and is finite separated. A point-equivalence predicate says that an additive equivalence from its existing coherent Grothendieck group to the existing representation group takes every associated bundle to the class of its rational module. The cohomology vector space is the existing Zariski $H^q(X,M)$ with scalar action through the structure morphism. These are data and predicates, with no existence assertion for a model, a restriction, an equivalence or a pushforward.
